# DotEnvUp

> DotEnvUp is an open-source encrypted .env file format (.env.up) and tooling ecosystem for developers.

## What is DotEnvUp?

DotEnvUp encrypts .env files into .env.up files that are safe to commit to Git. It uses hybrid public-key encryption (X25519 + XChaCha20-Poly1305) with zero-knowledge design — no server, no cloud, no key management service.

The .env.up format is a "half-open envelope": key names, versions, timestamps, and authors are visible in cleartext (replacing .env.example), while secret values are encrypted.

## Key Features

- Zero-knowledge encryption: Private keys stay on your machine (~/.dotenvup/identity)
- Safe to commit: .env.up files belong in Git
- Comments preserved: Lossless roundtrip of comments, blank lines, and structure
- Multi-recipient: Encrypt for multiple users (@alice, @bob) and machines (@ci)
- CI/CD ready: `up run -- npm test` decrypts at runtime with no file on disk
- Zero code changes: Works with existing dotenv libraries and process.env
- VS Code / Cursor extension: One-click lock/unlock; Partially protected when both .env and .env.up exist; Edit with DotEnvUp (Safe Edit) for in-memory edit without plaintext on disk; merge on unlock/Safe Edit
- CLI tool: `up init`, `up import`, `up lock`, `up unlock`, `up run`

## Format Specification

The .env.up format is a published open standard (v1):
- Full spec: https://github.com/sarhej/dotenvup/blob/main/docs/FORMAT_SPEC.md
- Encryption: X25519 key exchange + XChaCha20-Poly1305 (AEAD)
- Library: libsodium
- Multi-recipient via crypto_box_seal (anonymous sender encryption)

## Installation

```bash
# CLI
npm install -g @dotenvup/cli

# VS Code / Cursor extension
# Download .vsix from https://github.com/sarhej/dotenvup/releases
code --install-extension dotenvup-0.4.5.vsix

# Node.js library (drop-in dotenv replacement)
npm install @dotenvup/node
```

## Quick Start

```bash
up init            # Generate keypair (stored at ~/.dotenvup/identity)
up import .env     # Encrypt .env → .env.up (comments preserved)
up lock            # Delete plaintext .env
up unlock 5m       # Decrypt for 5 minutes
up run -- npm start  # Run with decrypted env vars (no file on disk)
```
